subject: MAP perf checkpoint: latency & throughput review
messages:
From: Diego Perez <dperez@healixhealth.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP week 6 perf snapshot – initial results

Karthik, team —

Attaching the raw numbers from our run this morning (healix_perf_summary_20260503.csv) and a quick set of latency plots (latency_plots_may3.pdf). High-level notes:

- Test harness: 4 clients with synthetic prompt mix (avg seq len 512) hitting rtx-a100-32G pool via your hosted endpoint.
- Throughput observed: ~860 tokens/sec sustained, P50 latency 180ms, P95 470ms for 1k token responses.
- When we enabled batching=16 we saw throughput spike to ~1,600 tokens/sec but tail latency increased (P95 ~1.1s).
- KV cache reuse is ~62% on our traces — looks like cold-starts are still common for some request paths.

We flagged two regression patterns in the CSV: a recurring spike around 09:00–09:15 local that correlates with another internal job on our side (we can exclude if helpful).

Next steps from our side: happy to join a quick sync to align on tuning priorities. Ideally we close MAP week 6 with an owners list for latency fixes and an expected impact estimate.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Perez
Lead ML Engineer — Healix Health

Karthik / Diego — I can do 1pm PT. Skimming the attachments, a couple of items to call out before the sync:

- Batching: If Healix expects many concurrent short chats (seq len < 256) we should recommend a dynamic batch policy that drops to batch=4 for tail-sensitive routes.
- KV cache: We should push a quick change to increase the prefix match window in the cache policy (reduce expiration from 5min -> 10min) for the customer’s workload — estimate ~6% P95 improvement in our profile.
- Quantization/variant: For heavy throughput routes we can propose an int8 variant (1% accuracy delta in our evals) that regains ~30% throughput at similar latency.

I'll bring sample config diffs to the call and mark the pieces that are canaries vs. full rollout.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

- KV cache window increase -> est P95 reduction 5-8% (low risk)
- Dynamic batch policy on tail routes -> est P95 reduction 8-12% while preserving throughput for bulk routes
- int8 canary -> throughput +28–32%, expected avg latency slightly lower for heavy routes; potential eval delta ~1% on our accuracy test set.

Consolidated action items (owners + dates):
- Marissa: int8 canary config + blurb in MAP doc (due 2026-05-05)

- Diego (Healix): confirm if the 09:00 internal job can be excluded or shifted (due 2026-05-04)

Next checkpoint: Fri 2026-05-07 quick stand to review canary numbers and decide rollout. If canary looks good we push a controlled rollout and update MAP closure ETA.
